label: 957-p1
verdict_reason: At TP4 rank shapes, by CUDA-graph replay, the replicated BF16 projection is not the PR's 2x win. With L2 hot (the PR's condition) the four owner layers' projection is 3.0-3.6 us a step lower at 1-6 rows and 2.4-8.3 us higher at 16, 32 and 48 rows. With L2 cold it is 226-238 us a step higher at every row count. The PR's 103.6-107.6 -> 51.6-53.1 us came from an eager loop, which measures launches: eager reproduces it here (base 45-54 us a layer, candidate 17-18). On one GPU the full TP4-rank decode step is 0.23-0.35 ms (1.1-1.6%) slower at 1-4 requests and 2-8 rows, all beyond the interval, and the same at 16x32. The loss sits in the three ratio-2 owner layers and comes from the COMP L2 window. Outputs are bit-identical to TP1 (test passes) and the static cost is +23.4 MiB a rank.
rule: Performance change: it must improve its own metric beyond the interval, and no cell of its own bench on a serving shape may be slower. Interval rule as candidates 49-53's: faster when the slower candidate boot beats the faster base boot, slower when the faster candidate boot is slower than the slower base boot, else the same.

cause.summary: The replicated ratio-2 compressor weight (10.5 MB, against the 2.0 MB rank shard) is what the COMP L2 window prefetches. COMP is built with the WO budget (20 MB), so it takes the whole weight. Its fill is issued after Q-B and cannot finish before the compressor's split-K GEMM reads the weight. So the GEMM reads mostly from DRAM while the 10.5 MB fill and the 18.9 MB WO fill queued behind it compete for the same bandwidth. COMP + WO (29.4 MB) also exceeds the 24 MB L2, where the base's 20.9 MB fit.
evidence: one GPU, nsys: the loss is in the three ratio-2 owner layers (+77..+85 us each), with a small spill (+3 us a layer) into the rest. The ratio-1 owner layer, with a 5.2 MB COMP, is +6 us.
projection cells: the replicated GEMM is about as fast as the shard with L2 hot (-3 us a step at 1-6 rows), but +226-238 us a step when it reads from DRAM
dropping only the COMP window removes the whole one-GPU loss and leaves a 0.15-0.44 ms gain

TP3 (coordinator, candidate-54 on sp5): #961's small-batch grid loss is the L2 prefetch windows' size, and capping them recovers it. So on the testbed at small batch the prefetch stream is near the critical path, and every extra byte there costs. On one GPU it is not critical (join wait 0), which is why one GPU shows +0.24-0.35 ms where the testbed shows +1.6-1.8 ms.
ruled_out: the build host (sp1 grid attribution: candidate-56's image with candidate-54's code equals candidate-54's image)
an untuned or non-captured GEMM: (512, 5120) and (1024, 5120) have tuned SPLIT_BF16 decode tiles and declared split-K kernels; graph-hot cells are at par with the shard at small M
lost overlap behind the removed all-gather: on one GPU the all-gather stand-in is a copy, and the step still loses with COMP and gains without it, so the loss does not need the all-gather
cause.not_shown_on_one_gpu: The testbed's 5x larger loss (1.6-1.8 ms against 0.24-0.35 ms) depends on how the prefetch stream overlaps the RoCE all-reduces. A tp4-switched grid run must confirm the fix.

fix_direction.recommended: Keep the replicated weight, but stop COMP prefetching it whole. Give COMP its own budget instead of BUDGET_WO in DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.build_l2_prefetch (nvidia/model.py), e.g. a new VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_COMP_MB. Default it to the sharded bytes (about 2 MB), or 0 when fused_wkv_wgate is replicated and unpacked. One GPU's control (COMP dropped) measures this direction: 0.15-0.44 ms faster than candidate-54, with the 4 all-gathers gone on top on the testbed.
fix_direction.alternative: Replicate only for SP prefill, or by row count: decode keeps the sharded packed weight (2.0/1.0 MB, prefetched hot), and prefill and #956's SP projection read the replicated BF16 copy. The base already holds such a copy for ratio 1 (_sp_weight). Choosing by rows does not help, because the cold replicated read loses at every row count; only the L2-hot cells favour it at 1-8 rows. This option keeps the 4 all-gathers at decode.

env_answer.comp_only_cap: No existing setting caps COMP alone. COMP's plan uses BUDGET_WO, so VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_WO_MB caps WO and COMP together, slicing a segment's head. A COMP-sized value (VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_WO_MB=2) would also cut every layer's 18.9 MB WO window to 2 MB, so it is not a fix.
env_answer.tp3_caps_at_tp4: VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_WO_MB=15 VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_FFN_MB=12 VLLM_DS41_L2_PREFETCH_NEXT_MB=12 leave the 10.5 MB COMP window whole (it is under 15 MB). They trim WO 18.9 -> 15 MB, so COMP + WO is 25.5 MB, still over the 24 MB L2. They cut a step's prefetch from 2,298 to 1,690 MB, about 20 times the 29.7 MB 0795 adds. If the TP4 loss is the stream's total load near the critical path (the TP3 mechanism), the caps should recover most of it. If it is COMP's race with its own GEMM, they will not. One GPU can't decide this, since its prefetch is not critical.
env_answer.test_to_run: tp4-switched grid suite (candidate-48/grid-suite.json), ABBA in one session: candidate-56-no956 (957-p1 alone) and its no957p1-no956 control, each with the 15/12/12 caps, against the same pair without caps. The caps' effect on candidate-54 at TP4 is unknown: #961 made TP4's grid 3.7% faster at candidate-51, so caps may lose some of that.
